A.explanation: There is no horizontal force to keep it moving right because air resistance is negligible and weight acts vertically.

B.explanation: Velocity is tangential to the curved path and keeps turning downward, while the only force stays in a fixed direction.

C.explanation: The angle between the curved velocity and the fixed gravitational force changes continuously, so it is not always $90^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: With air resistance negligible, weight $W = mg$ is the only force and it acts vertically downwards throughout the fall.

hints: Notice the statement that air resistance is negligible for the stone thrown horizontally from the cliff.
Recall what single force remains on a projectile when there is no air drag, and which direction that field force always acts.
Compare the direction of the curved velocity along the path to the sea with the fixed direction of that remaining force.
walkthrough: Identify the given conditions: the stone has an initial horizontal velocity but after release it is in free flight with air resistance negligible.
State the force rule: with no contact forces and no drag, the only force on the stone is its weight $W = mg$ due to gravity.
Set up the motion argument: horizontally there is zero resultant force so horizontal velocity is constant, while vertically the weight produces a downward acceleration $g$.
Distinguish velocity from force: velocity is tangent to the curved path shown and gains a growing downward component, but the resultant force does not turn with the path.
Therefore the resultant force is constant and vertically downwards throughout the fall. This is option D
